learning_outcomes.text: Argues the relationships between teaching-learning-evaluation and formulates creative solutions for optimizing educational components.
Correlates specialized, psycho-pedagogical knowledge in carrying out instructional-educational activities in education and other educational activities.
Argues the formative potential of theories, principles, and didactic practices specific to the field.
Identifies the specific way children/students/youth learn, theories and paradigms of counseling and support regarding learning and their implications for teaching evaluation.
Analyzes and correlates psycho-pedagogical knowledge in continuous training activities for improving professional practices.
Identifies the level of prior acquisitions of children/students/youth, individual and group, and utilizes the data obtained in designing the educational process.
Identifies learning objectives in accordance with curricular documents, which support the development of each child/student/youth's potential.
Constructs authentic learning contexts, in an integrated manner, in which students utilize their life experiences and cognitive interests.
Participates periodically in continuous professional development activities, in relation to their own professional needs and local or national priorities.
Critically approaches the responsibilities of the teaching profession, highlighting the complexity of the educational process.
Develops creative and constructive attitudes in applying pedagogical design and principles.
Indicates the necessity of using varied resources for efficient teaching, supporting learning, and helping students in their autonomous use.
Communicates effectively by providing constructive feedback and supports active student involvement in their own learning process.
Defends/Respects the ethnic, socio-economic, linguistic, and religious diversity of students and their communities of origin and manages its implications for learning development.
Supports the socio-emotional and moral development of students.
Supports family/guardians to understand the expectations and role of the school, collaborating with them for the students' educational success.
Combines interrogative and reflective approaches regarding professional practice and engagement in professional training and continuous education activities.

Displays/Manifests professional balance and adaptability in different contexts, including new or stressful situations, while maintaining appropriate authority in relation to educational individuals/groups.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to the field of Educational Psychology. Educational Psychology as a science. Definition. Delimitation of the field of Educational Psychology. Status and role of the teacher. Status and role of the student.

Human Personality. Human psychic system. Factors of personality development. Constitutive, defining elements of personality. Factorial models of personality (Guilford, Garden). Processual models of personality (Freud, Erikson, Piaget). Characterization of school ages.
Stages of ontogenetic development. Conceptual delimitations. Explanatory theories of human development (cognitive development, moral development, psycho-social development).

Human learning and school learning. Learning in the context of human activities. Learning as a process. Forms of elementary learning: conditioning, association, imitation. Forms of verbal learning: learning notions and principles, problem-solving. Theories of learning. E-learning. Online learning.
Motivation for learning. Components of motivation. The process of motivation. Explanatory theories. Motivation for learning. Strategies for motivating students in online education.
Creativity at school age. Definition. Creativity as a process and as a product. Creative personality. The role of creativity in learning. Stimulating student creativity in online education.
Recapitulation and examination topics. Review of the main topics covered in the course. Discussion of examination topics.
Introduction to the field of educational psychology
Learning in the school environment applications

assessment_methods.method: Exam (systematic observation of students - individual/team assignments, case study report; summative evaluation test)

assessment_rules: The final grade is based on 50% for the exam component and 50% for the applications component. The exam evaluates completeness and correctness of knowledge, logical coherence, argumentation, analytical and interpretive capacity, originality, creativity, language assimilation, and data processing. The applications evaluate the ability to apply knowledge in practice, analysis, interpretation, originality, and creativity. A minimum final grade of 5 is required to pass the course.
